$comment: Rules as data — roadmap 'Content as data'. Values come from spec.md §4 (stats, species, classes), §5 (creation points), §7.1 (steps), §8.1 (levels and tiers). Shape is packages/shared/src/types/domain.ts RulesContent; where this file and the docs disagree, the TS type wins. levelXp holds the nine thresholds above level 1 — levelXp[n] is the total XP needed to reach level n+2, per levelForXp()/maxLevel() in packages/shared/src/rules.ts. The curve is superlinear on purpose (spec §8.1): level 2 costs 100 so it lands at the end of the first chapter ever played, and level 10 costs 1600. The doubled steps at 400/400 and 900/900 sit on the tier boundaries. Icons are short slugs, never file paths: the client resolves them to inline SVG so every element has an icon (spec §11).

armored.name: Shell-hided
armored.text: Armored things wear a hard shell. Gentle pokes just bounce off, so bring something with a big wallop.

thorny.name: Thorn-hided
thorny.text: Thorny things are covered in spikes. Whatever hits one hard should be ready for a poke.

skittish.name: Skittish
skittish.text: Skittish things spook easy. A soft voice and a slow step work better than a loud shout.

flier.name: Flier
flier.text: Fliers stay up in the air, out of reach. You need wings, or something that can fly, to catch them.

swarming.name: Swarming
swarming.text: Swarming things come in a crowd. Hitting one is easy. Hitting all of them is the hard part.

fiery.name: Fiery
fiery.text: Fiery things run hot and glow like campfires. Cool things are good against them, and warm hugs are not.

frozen.name: Frosty
frozen.text: Frosty things are cold all the way through. Something warm and bright will make them shiver.

slippery.name: Slippery
slippery.text: Slippery things are wet and wiggly. Grabbing one is like holding soap, so try a trick instead.

ghostly.name: Ghostly
ghostly.text: Ghostly things are made of light and old memories. Swords go right through, but kind magic can reach them.

hulking.name: Hulking
hulking.text: Hulking things are enormous and slow. They hit hard, so be ready for a big thump.

force.name: Force
force.text: lifting, pushing and breaking things with muscle

climb.name: Climb
climb.text: getting up and over high or steep places

charm.name: Charm
charm.text: talking a creature round with kindness and wit

swim.name: Swim
swim.text: crossing water without getting swept away

search.name: Search
search.text: looking closely to find what is hidden

edges.text: Creatures settle down around a unicorn, so talking them round is easier.
Thorns lean away from a unicorn, so thorny things have a hard time hitting.
A unicorn's horn glances off armor, so swings at armored things go astray.
Unicorns are gentle, not strong, so heaving and breaking is harder.
A dragonling is small but mighty, so heavy lifting is easier.
A dragonling can flap up high, so fliers are easy to reach.
A dragonling puffs little smoke clouds, so sneaking is harder.
Skittish things bolt when a dragonling snorts, so they are hard to hit.
A griffin is at home in the air, so fliers are easy to reach.
Griffins have wings and strong claws, so climbing is easy.
A griffin sees far from above, so finding hidden things is easier.
Griffins have light bones, so a straight fight with armored things is harder.
Wet feathers are heavy, so swimming is harder for a griffin.
Bigfoot is huge and strong, so lifting and breaking is easier.
Bigfoot holds the line, so armored things have a hard time hitting.
Bigfoot is big and loud, so sneaking is much harder.
Bigfoot is too big to catch all the little ones, so swarms are tricky.
Bigfoot has long, strong arms, so swimming is easier.
A kitsune is full of clever words, so talking a creature round is easier.
A kitsune is a trickster, so sneaking past is easier.
A kitsune's tricks fool skittish things, so they are easy to hit.
Kitsune are quick and clever, not heavy, so heaving things is harder.
A kitsune's tricks do not work on hard armor, so armored things are harder to hit.
A manticore's pounce is fast, so skittish things cannot bolt in time.
Manticores climb like big cats, so climbing is easier.
A manticore's pounce lands right in the thorns, so thorny things are harder to hit.
Manticores do not like getting wet, so swimming is harder.
A Thornguard swings heavy, so armored things take more of a dent.
A Thornguard plants their feet, so big things swing wide.
A Thornguard holds the line, so a swarm cannot surround them.
A Thornguard knows brambles, so thorny things have a hard time hitting.
A Thornguard stands firm against hot, fiery things.
A big swing cracks frozen things.
A Thornguard stays on the ground, so fliers are hard to reach.
Heavy swings miss slippery things.
A Thornguard clanks along, so skittish things spot them and bolt.
Swings pass right through ghostly things.
Storm of Blades finds the gaps in armor.
Twin Step dances around big, slow things.
A Duskrunner is quicker than skittish things.
A Duskrunner can catch slippery things before they wriggle away.
Twin Step lets a Duskrunner hop up after fliers.
Too many little ones means nowhere to dodge.
Thorns snag a Duskrunner's quick, light blades.
Icy ground makes quick feet slide.
Burst hits a whole swarm at once.
Burst lands from a safe distance, so thorns cannot touch it.
Burst's starlight shows ghostly things where to aim.
Burst lights up the whole sky, so fliers have nowhere to hide.
Slippery things lose their grip in a Starweaver's bright light.
Warm starlight melts frozen things.
Sparks only feed fiery things.
Big things single out a Starweaver, who is not built to take a hit.
A Songkeeper's tune calms skittish things down.
A cool, steady song takes the heat out of fiery things.
Songs carry through ghostly things.
A Songkeeper's steady tune keeps many tiny nips from landing.
A Songkeeper swings weakly at armored things.
Big things are hard for a Songkeeper to knock about.
A Songkeeper has no thick hide, so thorny things find a way in.
Frozen things do not listen to a song, so they are harder to hit.
A Songkeeper's voice does not carry well up high.
A Thornguard bigfoot is steady as a boulder against big, hard-hitting things.
A Thornguard dragonling digs in and heaves a little harder.
A Thornguard manticore knows where to put its paws among thorns.
A Duskrunner griffin swoops after fliers with Twin Step.
A Duskrunner manticore stalks quietly, so skittish things never see the pounce coming.
A Starweaver kitsune's fox-light shows what is hiding in the dark.
A Starweaver dragonling's Burst glows with dragon fire.
A Starweaver unicorn's Burst shines pure and bright on ghostly things.
A Songkeeper unicorn sings a gentle tune that wins creatures over.
A Songkeeper kitsune sings sly, sweet songs that talk creatures round.

encounterBands.$comment:
Enemy stat blocks, by band. The hero-side numbers are above (baseMaxHp, baseGuard, baseSteps); these are their counterpart, and they live together because retuning a fight should be one file. Canon says which band a creature is — a judgment about the world; this says what a band is worth — a judgment about balance. See docs/canon-contract.md D9.
Derived, not invented: a level-1 hero swings d20+2..4 against Guard 11, and the same die says how hard a hit lands (damageTier in encounter.ts): 2 for a graze, 3 (ATTACK_DAMAGE) for a hit 5 or more past the Guard, 5 for a natural 20. So a little under 2 a round each and about 5.5 for a party of three. Spec 7.1 tunes for four rounds, so stats.hp x usualCount wants to land in 18-30. The skirmisher row is the Bramblewisp that bramblewood-01.json has shipped since before any of this.

skirmisher.description: Fast and fragile, and there are usually three of them. Dies quickly, but gets to you first.

lurker.description: Waits, then hits. Harder to land a blow on than it looks, and quicker than it looks.

brute.description: Slow, heavy, and hard to move past. Takes a while to bring down and hits hard when it lands.

sentinel.description: The hardest thing in an ordinary fight. Slow, very well armored, and it does not leave.

legend.description: A designed encounter rather than an ordinary one. Whatever it is, it is the reason the chapter exists.
legend.$comment: No stats on purpose: a legendary beast is a designed encounter, not a rolled one, so it must author its own and can never be generated.

unicorn.name: Unicorn
unicorn.blurb: Gentle, stubborn, and impossible to scratch. Thorns lean away when a unicorn walks by.

passive.text: +1 Heart. You are the one everybody comes to when they are hurt.

worldAbility.name: Mend
worldAbility.text: Heal a small wound between fights, and walk through thorns and brambles without a scratch.

combatAction.name: Mending Light
combatAction.text: Touch a friend standing next to you. They get 3 HP back.

dragonling.name: Dragonling
dragonling.blurb: Small, warm, and much stronger than it looks. Wings still a little too big for it.

passive.text: +1 Might. Heavy things are just things.

worldAbility.name: Glide
worldAbility.text: Cross a gap, a chasm, or a river the party cannot walk around.

combatAction.name: Gliding Leap
combatAction.text: Sail over anything in your way and land on any open tile within 6 steps.

griffin.name: Griffin
griffin.blurb: Half eagle, half lion, all opinions. Sees the whole map before anyone else does.

passive.text: +1 Quick. You are usually already there.

worldAbility.name: Skyward
worldAbility.text: Fly up and show the party the path ahead, with its hazards and its treasure.

combatAction.name: Sky Watch
combatAction.text: Circle overhead and call out where the enemies are going. Every friend gets +2 on their next roll.

bigfoot.name: Bigfoot
bigfoot.blurb: Enormous, shy, and very good at hugs. Doors are a suggestion.

passive.text: +2 max HP. There is simply more of you.

worldAbility.name: Smash
worldAbility.text: Break a barrier, lift something enormous, or carry a friend who cannot walk.

combatAction.name: Ground Smash
combatAction.text: Slam both hands down. Every enemy next to you is shoved back 2 steps.

kitsune.name: Kitsune
kitsune.blurb: A fox with too many tails and a plan for everything. Nobody is quite sure how many tails.

passive.text: +1 Clever. You notice the thing nobody else noticed.

worldAbility.name: Beguile
worldAbility.text: Charm someone into helping, or slip past a guard without being seen.

combatAction.name: Fox Fire
combatAction.text: Little blue flames dance around one enemy. It is so busy watching them that it skips its next turn.

manticore.name: Manticore
manticore.blurb: Lion, wings, and a curling tail. Grumpy in the morning, loyal all day.

passive.text: +1 Quick. Nothing is really out of reach.

worldAbility.name: Leap
worldAbility.text: Reach a high ledge, or drop down from any height and land just fine.

combatAction.name: Pounce
combatAction.text: Jump to any open tile within 6 steps and attack the moment you land.

thornguard.name: Thornguard
thornguard.blurb: You stand in front. That is the whole job, and it is a big one.

signature.name: Brace
signature.text: Take a hit that was meant for a friend standing next to you.

3.name: Shove
3.text: Push an enemy back 2 steps and step into its place.

6.name: Bramble Wall
6.text: Grow thorns on two tiles. Enemies have to go around.

9.name: Unbreakable
9.text: Until your next turn, you and every friend beside you take 1 less damage from every hit.

duskrunner.name: Duskrunner
duskrunner.blurb: Everywhere at once, never where the trouble lands.

signature.name: First Strike
signature.text: Go before anybody else on the first round.

3.name: Vanish
3.text: Slip out of sight. The next enemy that swings at you misses.

6.name: Twin Step
6.text: Move, attack, and then move again.

9.name: Storm of Blades
9.text: Attack two different enemies standing next to you.

starweaver.name: Starweaver
starweaver.blurb: You pull little pieces of the sky down and put them where they are needed.

signature.name: Burst
signature.text: Hit every enemy inside a 2x2 square of tiles.

3.name: Glimmer
3.text: A friend anywhere on the board gets +2 on their next roll.

6.name: Tanglelight
6.text: Ribbons of light wrap one enemy. It cannot move on its next turn.

9.name: Starfall
9.text: Every enemy on the board takes 2 damage. Once per fight.

songkeeper.name: Songkeeper
songkeeper.blurb: You keep everybody standing, and you make it look like a hero move. Because it is.

signature.name: Rally
signature.text: Heal a friend or yourself, or lift a knocked-down friend back up from across the board.

3.name: Soothe
3.text: A friend, or you, within 4 steps gets 3 HP back.

6.name: Chorus
6.text: Every friend gets 2 HP back and +1 on their next roll.

9.name: Encore
9.text: A friend takes another action right now. Once per fight.

fittingStall.$comment: The Exchange's fitting stall (docs/class-mastery.md §1, #312): a new hero, one who has finished no chapter and not used it yet, may swap class here once, for free, to any class. It stands in Gemfall's opening scene at the Exchange, named here so Gemfall gets it without a Gemfall file changing. The narration introduces the keeper before the phone names her.
fittingStall.narration: Just inside the market gate is a fitting stall, hung all over with capes, hoods, bracers and little bells. The tailor is a frogfolk named Madame Tuck. She wears every hat she owns at once, in one tall wobbly stack, so she never loses one. "New in town?" she asks everybody who walks past. "Your first fitting is free. Try on a new class, or keep the one you have."
